labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE (de-bridged): MAME runs on the host, no QEMU/QMP, no guest OS, no exec channel. Frames drawshm->shm, keys ctlsock keymap, audio FIFO. Launcher stations/mame-native/x11-runtime.sh; reset=relaunch restores the golden savestate in /data/vms/streamhost/stations/macsys1/sta.

render.stationsManifestPrelude: # macsys1 (VMID 199) — Macintosh 128K, System 1.0 / Finder 1.0 (1984), host-native MAME mac128k.

museum.blurb: The Macintosh exactly as it shipped in January 1984: System 1.0 and Finder 1.0 on a 128 KB Mac, 512x342 in one bit, a flat MFS floppy whose folders are a Finder illusion, one application at a time — and MacWrite 1.0 and MacPaint 1.0 on the second 400 KB disk to show what 72 dpi was for.
museum.notes: Host-native station: MAME 0.289's mac128k runs on the host (drawshm frames, ctlsock keys + the VIA quadrature mouse on :MOUSE0/:MOUSE1/:MOUSE2, FIFO audio) — no bridge kiosk, no nspawn container, no guest OS to exec into. -flop1 is the original January 1984 Macintosh System Disk (System 1.0, version string 0.97, with Finder 1.0); -flop2 is the companion Write/Paint disk carrying MacWrite 1.0 and MacPaint 1.0, so both volumes mount as icons on the desktop. No hard disk and no network exist on this machine: MFS is flat (folders live only in the Finder's Desktop file) and AppleTalk is still a year away, so retronet is permanently out of scope. Earliest point of the classic Mac OS lineage in the hall — macos753 (System 7.5.3) and macos9 are the same Finder, twelve and fifteen years on; lisa is the sibling one year earlier, the same desktop at four times the price.

reset.mouse: MEASURED 2026-09-13 on the real fleet binary (sha256 583d07a0...). The Mac 128K has NO ADB: the quadrature mouse is read through the VIA and exposed by the driver's `macplus` input map as three TOP-LEVEL ioports (src/mame/apple/mac128.cpp:1403-1411) -- :MOUSE0 (IPT_BUTTON1, PORT_NAME "Mouse Button"), :MOUSE1 (IPT_MOUSE_X, 0xff), :MOUSE2 (IPT_MOUSE_Y, 0xff). With MAME_CTL_PTR_TAGS/BTN_NAMES set, ctlsock reports 'setup btns=1 axes=1 movea=0' -- movea=0 is the EXPECTED apple2e-style degraded mode (no host-readable cursor register, so MOVEA is open-loop dead reckoning). GAIN MEASURED by two calibration moves from the homed origin: MOVE 100 0 displaced the arrow 396 published px, MOVE 0 100 displaced it 396 px -- 3.96 px/count on BOTH axes (the Mac's 512x342 raster at the 2x integer scale the 1024x768 surface letterboxes to 1024x684). Four-target MOVEA readback with GAIN_X=GAIN_Y=3.96, errors from fb-react.py bounding boxes: (300,200) -4,+4 | (700,500) 0,+8 | (150,600) -6,+8 | (850,150) +2,+2 -- worst 8 px. A CLICK WORKS: MOVEA onto the System Disk icon + CLICK1 inverted it (13604 px changed) and deselected Write/Paint. THE ONE OPEN ITEM IS A CONSTANT Y OFFSET, not drift: the 512x342 raster is letterboxed into 1024x768 as 1024x684 with a 42 px black band top and bottom, so the guest's cursor origin sits at published y=42 while the ctlsock module's belief origin is published y=0. Every landing is therefore 42 px BELOW the module's target (the four-target table above was aimed with that offset pre-subtracted), and the bottom ~84 px of the module's coordinate space is unreachable. Ships transport=none until that offset is carried in stream.pointer.offset and proven end-to-end from the real SPA. NEXT: set stream.pointer.offset=[0,-42] (or MAME_CTL_SCREEN to the letterboxed region) and re-run the four-target table aiming at raw surface coordinates.
reset.keyboard: MEASURED 2026-09-13 on the real fleet binary. The Macintosh keyboard is its own emulated device since MAME 0.221 -- an Intel 8021 MCU (romset mackbd_m0110, ip8021h_2173.bin, 1 KB) that debounces and clocks keycodes to the VIA over a synchronous serial line, NOT a CPU-scanned matrix, so MAME_CTL_KEY_EXCL is not expected and is not set; the station ships the fleet floor 40/40 ms. scripts/dev/mame-keymap.py --tags ':' generated 71 keys from KEYDUMP. TRAP: the mac128k default slot chain puts an M0120 numeric keypad IN FRONT of the keyboard, so every key field lives at ':kbd:pad:kbd:us:ROWn' (the keypad's own keys are at ':kbd:pad:ROWn') -- a keymap generated with the verb's default ':kbd:' tag filter finds nothing. SECOND TRAP: MAME's field names carry the shifted legend with DOUBLE spaces ('o  O', '1  !'), so a KEY verb spelled 'O' is rejected 'ERR noport'. PROOF: KEY down/up on ':kbd:pad:kbd:us:P2 Command' + ':kbd:pad:kbd:us:ROW5 o  O' produced 1900 changed pixels inside the selected icon's label -- the characters appeared on the framebuffer. (Finder 1.0 had put the label in rename mode from the preceding click, so the keystrokes landed as text rather than as the Command-O shortcut; the proof that keys REACH the guest and are RENDERED stands either way. That the rename was possible at all is why both floppies now ship mode 444 -- see the fixture.)
reset.fixture: Macintosh 128K at the Finder 1.0 desktop with BOTH 400K volumes mounted -- 'System Disk' (System Software 1.0 / Finder 1.0, January 1984) in the internal drive and 'Write/Paint' (MacPaint 1.0 + MacWrite 1.0) in the external -- plus the Trash and the Apple/File/Edit/View/Special menu bar, drawn at 512x342 1-bit and letterboxed at the 2x integer scale (1024x684) inside the published 1024x768 surface by MAME 0.289's mac128k running HOST-NATIVE (drawshm). MEASURED 2026-09-13: a cold boot takes ~37 s of wall time to the desktop ('Welcome to Macintosh.' at ~12 s), the golden savestate (63068 bytes, written in 27 ms) restores it in 2.4 s across a relaunch, and the restored frame is the cold-boot desktop. Reset is a relaunch with -state golden. BOTH DiskCopy 4.2 images are installed mode 444 (write-protected) on purpose: Finder 1.0 lets a click on an icon's label rename the volume, which a writable image would persist across every visitor.
